scope: Connector assembly with globally unique positional completion
known_limitations: When an answer cannot be proved unique, transform raises AssemblyError ('ambiguous', 'budget_exhausted', 'no_solution', 'parse_ambiguous', 'no_anchor' or 'bad_input') rather than returning a grid. A harness that expects a grid for every input will record these cases as failures.

The node budget (20000 per rule level) and render cap (8) are fixed. Pathological dense scenes may report budget_exhausted even when a unique assembly exists. Worst-case runtime in pure Python could reach several seconds.

The joint-grammar fallback is a stronger rule inferred from the generator's construction constraints. If the true task allowed reds to be met at a right angle, or allowed same-colour bodies to touch, that fallback could reject the intended assembly. It is used only after the positional rule fails to prove uniqueness.

Background is taken as the most frequent colour, with 0 preferred on ties. Red is fixed as 2 and the anchor as yellow 4, following the task. Inputs that break these conventions are rejected rather than reinterpreted.

Connector ownership relies on 4-adjacency, with a unique-nearest fallback. Pieces that touch each other in the input are separated by colour only. Two touching pieces of the same colour would be merged into one piece, which the generator never produces.

findings: Scope: only the cbebaa4b generator, explanation and fixtures were supplied. No constructor, explanation or fixtures were provided for d8e07eb2 (catalogue-driven joint piece assembly) or faa9f03d (intersecting five-path layer precedence with redirected rays). I therefore make no claims about those two tasks, and this solver does not cover them.

Rule as executed by the solver: pieces are the 4-connected components of each single non-background, non-red colour. Each red cell belongs to the unique piece it 4-touches; if it touches none, it goes to the unique nearest piece. The anchor is the largest yellow component and stays fixed. Every other piece is translated without rotation or recolouring. A piece is placed only when at least one of its reds lands on an open socket. Its body must avoid occupied cells and all red cells. Its reds must avoid occupied bodies and already merged reds. Matching reds merge; the remaining reds become new open sockets. The assembly is complete when every piece is placed and no socket is open.

Uniqueness handling: the positional search is exhaustive. It branches on the most-constrained socket, uses the remaining-red bound and the empty-cover forward check, collapses identical pieces, and counts distinct renders. Outcomes are explicit: exactly one render with the search finished gives 'unique'; two or more renders, or hitting the render cap, gives 'ambiguous'; exceeding the node budget gives 'budget_exhausted'. The solver never returns the first-found assembly as the reference program does.

The generator enforces a joint grammar during construction, but its own uniqueness certificate ignores it. The grammar rules are: a matched red lies between its two bodies in a straight line; bodies never touch a foreign red; bodies of the same colour never touch. The generator certifies uniqueness under the weaker purely positional rule. The solver uses the grammar only as a second, explicitly reported rule level ('unique_under_joint_grammar'). It applies only when the positional rule is not proved unique. Every generator-certified scene is unique positionally, so that path never changes their answer. The reason for this level is that the canonical fixtures were replayed through pieces=..., which renders them without validation, so their positional uniqueness is not certified by the generator.

Generator restrictions relative to the actual task: there is no rotation or reflection. The anchor is always a solid yellow rectangle of 3-4 x 3-5. Each non-anchor piece closes exactly 2 sockets (a docker) or exactly 1 socket while opening none (a leaf). Pieces that close 3 or more sockets, and single-connector pieces that open further sockets, are never produced, although the positional rule permits them. Bodies are 1-thick with no 2x2 block and no enclosed hole. In the input, pieces are scattered at Chebyshev distance >= 2, so connector ownership is always trivial. Real or adversarial inputs could place a red next to two pieces; the solver raises parse_ambiguous in that case rather than guessing.

Search budget: the generator certifies each scene within MAX_NODES=5000 nodes. The solver uses the same socket-selection order with tie-breaking by sorted socket coordinates, and the same identical-piece collapsing. On a positionally certified scene its exhaustive tree should therefore stay within a similar node count; it allows 20000 nodes. Branch order (most matches first) affects only how early solutions are found, not the size of the exhaustive tree.

Mechanism coverage: the static greedy-safety guard and the leaf-uniqueness prefilter are redundant with the final exhaustive check for correctness. They do bias the distribution, because they remove scenes containing decoy placements that a most-matches-first greedy assembler would accept. Fresh generator scenes are therefore easier than adversarial scenes for greedy solvers, but not for this exhaustive solver.

Plausible counterexamples the generator cannot emit, and how the solver treats them: (a) a sub-assembly whose pieces pair only with each other and never touch the anchor chain is rejected, because every placement must close a currently open socket; (b) a red that three pieces want to share is rejected, because merged reds are closed; (c) two yellow components of equal size cause an explicit parse_ambiguous error; (d) a piece with no reds can never be placed and yields no_solution.

Canonical labels are preserved unchanged. I have not executed the solver on the fixtures. In particular, I have not verified that the two query fixtures are positionally unique. If either is not, the joint-grammar level is expected to resolve it; if that also fails, the solver raises 'ambiguous' instead of altering or guessing a label.
semantic_review.execution_evidence: 1000 fresh unique inputs matched independent solver and archived solver; canonical fixture outputs unchanged.
